_comment: SecOpent curated seccomp profile (M5 Phase 2.5). Strategy: denylist (defaultAction=SCMP_ACT_ALLOW) with explicit SCMP_ACT_ERRNO denies for high-risk syscalls. This is STRICTLY ADDITIVE hardening on top of Docker's default profile (~60 syscalls blocked): we additionally deny bpf, keyctl, open_by_handle_at, clone3, and others that Docker's default still permits. An allowlist (~300 syscalls) was rejected because (a) strace-based per-adapter syscall collection is Linux-only and DEFERRED (cannot validate on Windows), and (b) a missing syscall would silently break adapter compatibility. The denylist cannot regress adapters: any syscall not in the denylist behaves exactly as Docker's default. To tighten further, run `strace -ff -e trace=%file,%network,%process <adapter>` on Linux per adapter and convert this to an allowlist. Apply with: docker run --security-opt seccomp=scripts/provision/secopent-seccomp.json
